262K likes, 2,137 comments - prattprattpratt on October 29, 2026: "Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company. One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, “Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?”

She asked if I could act, and I said, “Fuck yeah, put me in your movie!”

She asked for my phone number. The only problem was I didn’t have one. So I gave her my buddy Mike’s number instead. A couple days later, Mike casually mentions, “Oh, by the way, someone called you.” ARE YOU KIDDING ME, MIKE?!

I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious. I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character’s name was Devon, and I remember thinking, “Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!”

I showed up to the audition with every line and inflection mapped out in pencil. Rae told me I could act and offered me the part. I asked if we were shooting in Hawaii. Nope. Los Angeles.

I had about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades.

Then Rae told me they’d fly me out. And I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I’m going to be an actor.

That little movie was Cursed Part 3, a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me.

I’ll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me.".

83K likes, 590 comments - prattprattpratt on October 28, 2026: "Happy 50th birthday to my big brother. My hero. Cully Pratt.

When I was a kid I wanted to be just like Cully. I used to wear his clothes the day after he did, picked em right up off his floor and put them on because they smelled so good and he knew how to match. Haha. I looked up to him that much. He played Boo Bear in the Christmas Play and that made me want to be an actor. Truth is, I don’t think there’s a single part of the man I am today that wasn’t shaped in some way by him.

He’s an incredible artist. A craftsman. A father. He served his country in the Army and his community in law enforcement. But those are just things he’s done. Who he is, is a good man. A really good man.

Life gets busy. We don’t spend nearly as much time together as we used to. I miss that. I miss being kids. I miss looking up to him every day. Funny thing is, I still do.
I love you, brother. More than I probably tell you. You were my first hero. Fifty years on this earth and I’m so grateful I got to spend mine being your little brother.

Happy Birthday Bro!".
